long_description:
Erskine Chapel Open Day
See the splendid beauty of Erskine Chapel (Sacré Coeur), tucked away in the hills of Island Bay.

Erskine Chapel is an iconic Category 1-listed French Gothic chapel, a sentinel of older times. Located in the core of the former Erskine College building, the chapel’s interior is of great significance.

In 2023, significant strengthening and restoration works were completed on the chapel, including the west façade and entrance, major steel structural upgrades, and a new roof. The chapel is located on the first level, where the restoration reaches a full crescendo of white arched ceilings lit by stained glass. No effort was spared to return the interiors to their original beauty, despite a decade of severe neglect.

Erskine Chapel won the heritage category of the Te Kāhui Whaihanga New Zealand Institute of Architects (NZIA) 2024 Awards, highlighting the work of Tobin Smith of Common Architecture and Adam Wild of Archifact Architecture & Conservation Heritage.

Mark this date in your calendar now and experience the chapel's charm and restored beauty.

Cost: Entry to chapel by Koha for ongoing chapel maintenance.

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/erskine-chapel/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
Please park on nearby streets. Only vehicles with accessibility needs are allowed entry to the complex.
For those driving through, please drive slowly and remain watchful for children and pets.
When leaving the chapel, check for cars. Do not walk on the road and keep to the left of Avon Street.
The lift swings outwards. Please avoid standing within the yellow marked lines.

Upside Down! Inversion Workshop with Kathleen Kuehn
We get our hearts above our head in this workshop focused on inverted postures - think headstand, handstand and forearm stand! It'll be playful, strong but accessible with loads of options, technique and practice for everyone present.

We'll prep the body for these poses first, then move into the mechanics of each before giving them a go. Expect individualised attention, specific cueing and optional hands-on assists (with consent) to get you upside down!

You'll also get some great takeaway exercises to work on at home if you want to continue the inversion journey!

Why inversions?

Inversions have a host of benefits: they can improve circulation, lymphatic drainage and mental focus; build strength; stimulate digestion and more! But most of all, they're just a lot of fun!

Who is this for?
This workshop is suitable for most levels of practice; you don't need to be an expert, but you'll want at least a few asana classes under your belt. That said, everything you need to know will be offered on the day!

CYTs can also earn 3 CE credits with Yoga Alliance.

This workshop will be capped to keep it manageable -- enrol now so you don't miss out!

About the Facilitator

Kathleen Kuehn (E-RYT 500) who enjoys playful vinyasa classes, challenging asana and stringing them together in creative ways. Anatomy and alignment lover. Can't actually do a handstand herself, but can 100% talk you into getting into (and falling out of!) one yourself in a safe way!

long_description:
The Triple Swing Bill | Wellington Jazz Festival
The Guiding Tones, Arēki Trio and Uncle Chipper are teaming up this Wellington Jazz Festival to bring you a triple-header afternoon of swing at the iconic Old St Paul's!

The Guiding Tones is an unconventional jazz trio based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Consisting of Vadim Fong on clarinet, Zylah Vivace on guitar and Joseph Coleman on piano accordion, they bring unique instrumentation and a fresh voice to classic swing repertoire. The group plays a range of material, focusing mainly on swing music à la Duke Ellington, but also branching into jazz manouche and even bebop.

Arēki Trio is also based in Wellington and features Alex Christensen on guitar, Ned Rainey on drums, and Mathieu Ornberg on bass. The trio formed in their first year at Te Kōkī / New Zealand School of Music through their shared studies in jazz, and continue to create music together. The trio plays a range of music, including classic ballads, modern jazz, and atmospheric pieces aiming to create an environment where grooving rhythms and improvisation flow.

This group endeavours to make Uncle Chipper proud through their performance of various elegant jazz tunes. Come along to witness this flock of friends experimenting with collaborative ideas. Max Stopyra will be in attendance, holding down the bass lines. Sascha Hunt will be too, but more in the strumming department. Ranu Wijesuriya and his cymbal (+ kit) will collaborate with the aforementioned Max to groove. Logan Heppell will oversee the department of ivory tickling, while Sylvester Green will add elements of melody at times.

The Wellington Jazz Festival is on 14-18 October.

Tickets are on sale from Wednesday 2 September with pricing starting at $10.

name: Sulfate - Live at Meow - And It Wants Album Release Tour

long_description:
Sulfate - Live at Meow - And It Wants Album Release Tour
Feral, devolved and running on instinct, the six songs on Sulfate’s third album ‘And It Wants’ grapple between David Harris unleashing on his drum kit, Zac Arnold conjuring fuzz and feedback and Peter Ruddell’s taut, wiry guitar-work and commanding baritone. Written and recorded in New Lynn’s industrial area, this new batch of songs were created on a diet of Cormac McCarthy novels, Adam Curtis documentaries and the madness of gothic horror. Since recording, Sulfate's line up has expanded once more, introducing multi-instrumentalist Louisa Nicklin to the band's inexorable live performances.

Sonically, Sulfate set out some parameters at the outset of the album recordings - and it was important for things to sound real. The band wanted real instruments to be played, and, importantly, sound like they’re being played, by real, living people. This was a conscious reaction to the modern, online, perfect-existence, social media-ness of it all. Audio engineer Emily Wheatcroft-Snape was recommended to the band because of her ability to capture sounds with accuracy and precision - and she encapsulated the live band just as they had hoped.

Thematically, ‘And It Wants’ sees Ruddell clinging to optimism and joy while being subject to the existential nihilism of our current hypernormal, western reality. “Death is all through this record. The songs were born out of the feeling that there are no rules, that nothing matters, and that we all die. That we dance around the fact that death comes for us all, but we never really, truly, acknowledge it - it’s just too big or too heavy to have any kind of impact on our day to day existence. The intent is to provide a sonic backdrop to dance ecstatically, liberated, as the world around you burns. Find comfort and joy in things while you can, even as the end draws near and darkness begins to ruminate.”

‘And It Wants’ is out digitally, and on two exclusive vinyl variants via Flying Nun Records and Holiday Records on October 23rd.

3 hour workshop, Movement ~ Breathwork ~ Sound Journey

Saxon Brazier from Grounded Grace Counselling and Kez Milne from Alchemy Ascending bring you a 3-hour immersive workshop combining Somatic Movement, Conscious Connected Breathwork and Sound Odyssey.

A deep dive into the body — creating space to slow down, rest, digest and reconnect with what is happening beneath the surface.

You might arrive carrying stress, emotions, old hurts, tension, overwhelm or simply the weight of everyday life.

Through conscious connected breathwork, somatic movement and sound, we create a safe and supported space to explore what your body may be holding — without needing to force, fix or figure anything out.


🌿 CONSCIOUS CONNECTED BREATHWORK

Conscious Connected Breathwork is a rhythmic breathing practice where the inhale and exhale are intentionally connected, creating a continuous flow of breath without pause.

As we consciously connect the breath, we bring greater awareness into the body. Physical sensations, emotions, thoughts and patterns may begin to come into awareness, creating space to notice and explore what is present.

Rather than trying to think our way through an experience, the breath invites us to move out of the thinking mind and into the body — meeting whatever arises with curiosity, awareness and compassion.

The practice is centred around presence and allowing, rather than forcing an emotional release or trying to create a particular outcome.


🎶 SOUND ODYSSEY

Following the breathwork, Saxon's Sound Odyssey will invite you into a deeply immersive sound experience designed to help you settle, integrate and reconnect with the body.

Having previously sold out her Sound Odyssey experiences, Saxon weaves together drums, medicine drum, guitar and vocals to create a rich and organic soundscape.

Moving from rhythm and activation into softer, settling vibrations, the sound journey offers space to simply lie back, breathe and receive.

A meeting point of sound, vibration, voice and stillness — allowing the body and nervous system time to integrate whatever has arisen during the breathwork.


✨ YOUR FACILITATORS

Kez Milne — Alchemy Ascending
400-hour accredited Conscious Connected Breathwork Facilitator.

Saxon Brazier — Grounded Grace Counselling
Registered trauma-informed counsellor with training in breathwork and somatic facilitation.
https://www.groundedgrace.nz/

Together, Saxon and Kez will hold a grounded, carefully facilitated container for you to explore breath, body, emotion and sound.


⚠️ SAFETY & CONTRAINDICATIONS

Safety is paramount. Breathwork is not suitable for everyone.

Conscious Connected Breathwork involves sustained, active breathing and can produce significant physical and emotional experiences. For this reason, there are certain circumstances where participation may not be appropriate.

This workshop may not be suitable for you if you:

• Are pregnant or may be pregnant
• Have a history of cardiovascular disease, heart attack or significant heart problems
• Have uncontrolled high blood pressure
• Have a history of stroke, aneurysm or significant vascular disease
• Have epilepsy or a seizure disorder
• Have severe or uncontrolled asthma or significant respiratory disease
• Have a current serious psychiatric condition, psychosis or significant difficulty distinguishing internal experiences from external reality
• Are experiencing acute psychological distress or significant mental health instability
• Have recently undergone major surgery or have another significant medical condition that may make intensive breathwork unsafe
• Are under the influence of alcohol or recreational drugs
• Have another medical or psychological condition that may make an intensive breathwork practice unsafe for you

If you are unsure whether this practice is appropriate for you, please speak with your doctor or qualified healthcare professional before booking.

Participation is voluntary and you can stop or modify the practice at any time.

Every participant will be required to read the full disclaimer and contraindications and sign a waiver confirming that they understand and agree to the terms before entering the workshop space.

We take the responsibility of holding this space seriously. Safety, consent, choice and nervous-system awareness are paramount throughout the experience.


🌿 BOOKING & ONBOARDING

Once your booking has been made, we will send you a full onboarding pack with everything you need to know before the workshop, including what to bring, how to prepare and important instructions for arriving and entering the space.

LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
Calling all those who want to level up their Lindy! We have a special two week crash-course designed specifically for those who want to make the jump from beginner to intermediate (and those who want to brush up on their skills)!

Basically, if you're wanting to move up in your Lindy journey but not sure how to get there, these open-level workshops are for you!*

They’re also a great option for any intermediate dancers who want to build a solid foundation for 2027 and beyond, or for those who want to try switching leading/following!

Week 1 | Nov 10, 6:30pm-8:45pm: Swing-out deep-dive

Swing-outs are one of the fundamental moves that make Lindy-Hop, well, Lindy-Hop! They're awesome but can be tricky to master (journey not a destination!) In this 2h workshop we'll hone in on the craft and techniques that make swing-outs feel oh-so good, as well as introduce some fun styling and variations you can incorporate to make them your own!

Week 2 | Nov 17; 6.30pm-8:45pm: Improver essentials

Switching between the fundamental Lindy footwork can be a challenge! This 2h workshop is designed to build your confidence in moving between 6-count, 8-count and Charleston. On top of this, we'll be focusing on expanding your dance vocabulary so you can hit the social dance floor with style!

*For beginners who come to both workshops you’ll (pretty much) be ready to join intermediate classes in 2026! (Please still check in with the facilitators before committing to intermediate classes).

Join the Wellington Pride Festival for a fundraising screening of 'La Bola Negra' on 15 October at the Penthouse Cinema in Brooklyn.

LA BOLA NEGRA tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and inheritance, across three different eras - 1932, 1937, and 2017.

- Winner, Festival De Cannes: Best Director
- "A work of staggering genius" - Indiewire.com
- "Extraordinary" - Deadline

- The film is in Spanish and will also be screened with English captions
- The theatre is wheelchair accessible and wheelchair accessible bathrooms are available
- Parking is available right next door in the Penthouse carpark
- You are more than welcome to wear a mask.

Tickets $25 waged, $20 low or unwaged. Your money goes to supporting the Wellington Pride Festival, Aotearoa's longest-running Pride Festival.

A healthy microbiome supports ECS signaling (via microbial metabolites and fatty acid precursors), which can help alleviate anxiety, depression symptoms, and anhedonia (lack of pleasure/motivation), creating a virtuous cycle for brain and gut health.

Whether you're seeking preventive wellness, mood optimization, or support for persistent challenges, this gut-centric, neuroscience-informed approach — rooted in wholefoods and ancient remedies — helps you unlock your body's innate healing potential from the inside out.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

Tom Jones is a retelling of Henry Fielding's comic novel, a bawdy tale of 18th century virtue and villainy, in a musical setting by Edward German. An operetta is a comic opera with dialogue, just like musical theatre (but without microphones). Operettas are what came before classic musicals such as The Sound of Music. An operetta can be performed with small orchestra or piano, and does not necessarily require operatic singers. We encourage all confident singers to audition.

long_description:
Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer | Wellington (Late Show)
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

"Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set," says Tonnon. "It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui."

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video "Executive Assistant" offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8.45PM I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

Natural Textured Rings - November Taster!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 till 4 October.

Circa Theatre Behind the Scenes Tour
Discover the 50-year history of Circa Theatre with a 1-hour guided tour of Wellington’s foyer and backstage area at this historical building on the waterfront.

As a leader of arts and culture in Wellington, Circa Theatre brings quality playwriting and performance to the Capital's glorious waterfront. Discover and celebrate the 50-year history of Wellington’s iconic Circa Theatre with a 1-hour guided tour of Wellington’s foyer and backstage area at this historical building on the waterfront.
You will be taken on a unique guided tour of this historic building, including the back of house, which is usually actors only! Learn about the fascinating building move from 7 Harris Street to 1 Taranaki Street – including how the facade of 120-year-old Westport Chambers was trucked across the road and the new theatre built in behind it.

Walking tour with stairs to the upper floor. Working theatre, can include moving props and people. Please wear good shoes and dress for the weather. The tour may be cancelled in bad weather.

long_description:
👑 ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ — ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ 👑 Maharani Jindan- The Last Queen of Punjab
👑 ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ — ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ 👑
🔥 ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ੇਰਨੀ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ… ਜਿਸਨੂੰ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਕਦੇ ਭੁਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ! 🔥

ਉਹ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ…
ਉਹ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਧੀ, ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ, ਇੱਕ ਯੋਧਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੌਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਸੀ। ❤️

ਜਦੋਂ ਹਾਲਾਤਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਝੁਕਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕੀਤੀ, ਉਹ ਹੋਰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਹੋਈ।
ਜਦੋਂ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਉਸਦਾ ਪੁੱਤਰ, ਉਸਦਾ ਰਾਜ ਅਤੇ ਉਸਦੀ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦੂਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਲਈ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਘਰਸ਼ ਦੀ ਅੱਗ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੁਝੀ।

⚔️ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦ ਕੌਰ — ਸ਼ੇਰ-ਏ-ਪੰਜਾਬ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਦਲੀਪ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ — ਦੀ ਇਹ ਗਾਥਾ ਸਾਡੀ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਪੀੜ੍ਹੀ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।

🎭 Rang Manch Karee Theatre Group Melbourne ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ, ਸੰਘਰਸ਼, ਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਮਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰਤੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਪਿਆਰ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵੰਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਚ ’ਤੇ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।

🇳🇿 ਹੁਣ ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਨਾਟਕ Wellington ਵਿੱਚ!

📅 ਐਤਵਾਰ, 7 ਮਾਰਚ 2027
📍 Little Theatre, Lower Hutt, Wellington

❤️ ਆਓ ਆਪਣੇ ਬੱਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਆਈਏ।
ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸੀਏ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਮਹਾਰਾਜੇ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਵੀ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਰਚਿਆ ਹੈ।

✨ ਇਹ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਟਕ ਨਹੀਂ…
ਇਹ ਸਾਡੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ਼ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਦਰਦ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਔਰਤ ਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੌਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੇਰਨੀ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਾਸਤਾਨ ਹੈ। 👑🔥

🙏 ਇਸ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਾਰੀ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਬਣੋ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਸੁਨੇਹੇ ਨੂੰ ਵੱਧ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ।

📞 ਆਪਣੇ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ੋਅ ਕਰਵਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਸਾਡੀ ਟੀਮ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

CAT POWER
THE GREATEST. ON TOUR.

This November, Cat Power returns to Aotearoa, New Zealand for the first time since 2014 for three special shows: Thursday 26th November at Auckland’s Bruce Mason Centre, Friday 27th November at Wellington’s Opera House and now Saturday 28th November at Christchurch's James Hay Theatre. Cat Power will be performing her seminal album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular songbooks of the last three decades.

Twenty years on, Cat Power’s Memphis soul stirrer The Greatest is still one of the most astounding records ever to be heard, a late-night classic that still feels as intimate two decades after it first blew our minds and broke our hearts.

Support for these three shows will be Canterbury’s finest, Lawrence Arabia, performing an intimate solo set. Expect to hear some old favourites and new treats from his forthcoming album.

The Great Kāpiti Race 2027
🏁 THE GREAT KĀPITI RACE – SUNDAY 7 MARCH 2027 🏁

Kāpiti… THE RACE IS ON!

Grab your team and get ready for a day of clues, challenges, puzzles, mystery locations and probably a fair bit of ridiculousness as you make your way around the Kāpiti Coast.

Think adventure race meets treasure hunt — but this is NOT a fitness race! You don't need to be super fit, fast or particularly coordinated 😂 You just need a team that's ready to have some fun.

🗺️ HOW WILL IT WORK?
You'll start the day at our official starting point, where your team will receive your first clue.
Solve it correctly and it'll lead you to your next location somewhere around Kāpiti.

When you arrive, you might need to:
🧩 Solve a puzzle
🎯 Complete a challenge
🔎 Find something hidden
📸 Take a photo or video
🤪 Do something completely ridiculous
📍 Check in at a local business or location
🗺️ Work out where your next clue is sending you

Complete it and you're onto the next one!

Expect to discover local businesses, attractions, parks, sports facilities and places around Kāpiti you may never have visited before.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 WHO CAN ENTER?
Teams will be 2–5 people and kids are absolutely welcome!
This is designed to be something families, couples, friends and workmates can all do.

You will need your own vehicle to travel between some checkpoints, and at least one team member will need to be an adult.

📅 THE IMPORTANT STUFF
DATE: Sunday 7 March 2027
TIME: Approximately 10am–4pm
LOCATION: All around the Kāpiti Coast
TEAM SIZE: 2–5 people

🏆 AND YES… THERE WILL BE PRIZES!
We'll have major prizes, spot prizes and plenty of opportunities to win things throughout the day.
And winning won't necessarily just be about being the fastest. 👀

long_description:
WOW: Meet the Makers
Step inside the World of WearableArt® and hear from the people at the heart of the spectacle.

WOW: Meet the Makers is an inspiring evening of stories, creativity and insight, featuring some of the region's most accomplished WOW designers. Hear from 2026 Supreme WOW Award winner Kayla Christensen as she shares her journey to the top of the world's premier wearable art competition, alongside fellow Kāpiti designer Rebecca Bond, whose imaginative work has earned recognition on the WOW stage. Guests will also enjoy reflections from legendary WOW designer Fifi Colston, a 30-time entrant and multi-award winner whose extraordinary body of work has helped shape the competition's history.

Hosted by Sarah Nathan, Head of Competition for WOW, the evening offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at how a WOW entry evolves from an initial spark of inspiration to a world-class performance. Through designer conversations, creative storytelling and insights into the competition process, guests will discover what it takes to create work that captivates audiences and judges alike.

Whether you're a long-time WOW fan, an aspiring creative, or simply curious about the people behind the spectacle, this exclusive event offers a rare opportunity to connect with the makers, stories and artistry at the heart of WOW.


WOW: Meet the Makers is presented by Visit Kāpiti.

Your panel:
Sarah Nathan
Head of Competition
Gain a unique behind-the-scenes perspective on the WOW Competition as Sarah shares insights into artistic excellence, creative innovation, and what it takes for designers to stand out on the world stage.

Kayla Christiansen
Local Artist and WOW Supreme Award Winner 2026
Kayla Christiansen is a local artist with a passion for all things creative, from fine arts to wearable arts and everything in between. Join Kayla to hear about the journey to becoming a WOW Supreme Award winner and where here imagination is taking her for her next creative journey.

Fifi Colston
WOW Finalist Designer
Discover how storytelling, costume, and craftspersonship come together in wearable art as Fifi shares creative insights from three decades at WOW, revealing the imagination and process behind award-winning designs.

Rebecca Bond
Multidisciplinary Artist and WOW Designer
Kāpiti Coast based artist Rebecca Bond works across contemporary jewellery, silversmithing, wearable art, performance drawing and community arts. Hear Rebecca share insights from her creative journey inspired by people and nature and how her practice explores identity and connection.

Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Inspire Me!
Hooked: Navigating the Age of Dopamine




From endless scrolling and notifications to constant cravings for quick satisfaction, our minds are perpetually wired for the next hit. But why does chasing cheap dopamine leave us feeling so drained and distracted ?

​This interactive 1-hour workshop bridges modern psychology with timeless wisdom to help us break the loop.

Join us for a relaxed, interactive discussion where we explore how replacing cheap distractions with a "higher taste" can quiet the restless mind, reclaim focus, and unlock a deeper sense of fulfillment.







End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.



Meet your host Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

➡️Identify the biggest risks threatening family businesses and how to manage these risks.

➡️Provide practical advice on navigating conflict, succession planning, and fairness within the family.

➡️Discuss tools and processes for improving communication, trust, and decision-making across generations.

➡️Advise on how to set up appropriate family governance structures based on real family business experience and tested strategies.

Philip is a trusted advisor to family businesses, combining expertise in family psychology, change, and business consulting. Over the past 28 years, he has worked with family business owners and executives in London, New York, New Zealand, and Australia.

🎤Bob Selden

Bob Selden is a Senior Consultant with Family Business Central, helping family businesses across New Zealand strengthen leadership, manage transition and build lasting family and business legacies. Based in the Manawatu, Bob has been involved with Family Business Central since its establishment in New Zealand in 2017 and has led the New Zealand business since then. Prior to this, he and CEO Philip Pryor worked together for more than 20 years in Australia and overseas.

Vincents Annual Group Exhibition - Opening Night
Vincents Art Workshop presents

Annual Group Exhibition 2026

4 – 30 November
Vincents Gallery
Willis St Village, 5/148 Willis St
Opening night: Wednesday 4th November, 5:30pm–7:00pm

Nau mai, haere mai! Vincents Art Workshop warmly invites you to the opening of its Annual Group Exhibition 2026. Following the success of last year’s 40th Anniversary Exhibition at Tākina, this year’s celebration returns home to Vincents Gallery in the heart of Wellington’s CBD.
Step inside and discover a vibrant showcase of work by the talented artists who attend our inclusive community art studio—a welcoming space where people from all walks of life create side by side. Ka Mua, Ka Muri - Te Motu Kairangi
This exhibition looks at the early history of the Miramar Peninsula through the lens of estate agent and amateur archaeologist H. N. McLeod.

Hector McLeod stood atop the Miramar Cutting in 1910, on the site of the historic Maupuia Pā. The photograph he captured there and his subsequent annotations, notes, and articles on Māori local histories will be on display in Tō Tātou Pōneke, our new heritage space at Te Matapihi | Wellington Central Library. The exhibit will also explore the development of Miramar as a suburb, and McLeod's own brief time as Mayor of the Borough.

Railway Carriage Restoration Workshop
We are restoring three 120-years old railway carriages to as near their as-built condition as possible. The first is nearly completed.

An open day at our workshop, to view progress to date and work in progress.
Our carriages were built using recycled timber 1905-07 by the Wellington & Manawatu Railway Company based on North American plans. They are quite different in construction from any New Zealand Railways-built carriages. We have quite a few challenges to meet as we progress!

Booking is REQUIRED for this event.
